title: Understanding Decoding in Reading Development
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Title 

Talk 

Title Talk

summary:
**Decoding** is a foundational reading skill where students recognize letter sounds and blend them together to translate written words into speech. The process involves recognizing letters and patterns (like *b*, *sh*, *igh*), knowing their sounds, and blending them to read words (e.g., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes "cat"). 

**Reading Rockets** offers research-based decoding activities organized by grade level:
- **Kindergarten**: [Phonics and decoding activities](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101Kindergartener phonics and decoding activities)
- **First Grade**: [Phonics and decoding activities](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities)
- **Second Grade**: [Phonics and decoding activities](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities)
- **Third Grade**: A [video demonstration](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities) showing how 3rd graders use syllables to decode longer words

summary: The **Reading Corner** has published their January newsletter focusing on **reading fluency**. Fluency is the ability to read accurately, at an appropriate pace, and with expression. Families can help students increase fluency through regular reading and rereading of familiar books, practicing sight words in context, reading aloud with expression, and discussing stories. A helpful resource is **[Reading Rockets](https://www.readingrockets.org/)**, which offers family-friendly tips and videos. Contact Reading Corner instructors for questions: Mrs. Geshan at geshanc@talawanda.org, Mrs. Kobermann at kobermanc@talawanda.org, or Mrs. Walters at waltersh@talawanda.org.

title: Upper Parking Lot Restrictions Enforced
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
*PARKING 

REMINDER*

*PARKING REMINDER*

We know the weather is getting colder and it is covenient to park in the upper lot and wait for your student. However, this lot is reserved for staff and Preschool pick up ONLY. Starting MONDAY 12/8, the only vehicles we will be allowing in the upper lot at drop off and pick up will be those with the orange PRESCHOOL sheet in the window.This is to ensure the safety of our students that are walkers and foot pick up as well as our bus riders. We are seeing a large number of cars parking in the upper lot or blocking the busses which is causing traffic flow issuesWe appreciate your cooperation!If you have any questions or concerns, please call the office! We are happy to help!

summary: **Starting Monday, December 8**, only vehicles with an **orange PRESCHOOL sheet** will be allowed in the upper parking lot during drop-off and pick-up times. The upper lot is reserved for **staff and preschool pick-up only**. This policy ensures safety for walkers, foot pick-up students, and bus riders, and prevents traffic flow issues. Contact the office with questions.
